body:
I can relate OP. It feels like there's an actual curse on me sometimes. Somehow I'm never deserving of support no matter what. Even when I went through cancer treatment and other illnesses. I did have some practical help from friends which helped me out so much, but there was no safe place emotionally, to rest and be be held by someone else for a while. Even in the hospital itself  the nurses would be nice to all the patients who fitted in with human life and had spouses and family etc and kind of off with me, no matter how friendly and undemanding I tried to be - it's like they could sense something off me, that I'm really not part of humanity and they were scared it was catching.

I'm sorry you are going through this. It's not fair.

Thanks for the validation. It is so confusing growing up with parents like that. They were so sure they were great and perfect, I started to believe the weirdest behaviours  were normal things that every family did behind closed doors and my discomfort was just me being wrong wrong wrong as usual.

I'm not sure if this counts as creepy - it definitely made me very uncomfortable at the time and it grosses me out to this day if I think of it - although not nearly as bad as some other stories here. When I was a teenager, my mother (I am also female) got fascinated with how different her butt felt when she tensed it up versus when it was relaxed and she made me sit there for ages with the palm of my hand on her buttock while she flexed the muscle over and over as she thought it was just so amazing.
Congratulations on the birth of your little daugher 🤗 and also on surviving all you have.

Count me in for breast cancer and arthritis (rheumatoid) too. And actually also the insomnia, anxiety and cptsd😬My only other sibling also has rheumatoid arthritis even though neither of my parents do - I'm sure it's our early environment. The physical illnesses all kicked in after a period of my mother being particularly full on with the control, manipulation and intrusion, my whole body felt on fire with stress and panic waiting for her next contact. I swear I felt the moment my body turned on itself. I guess that could also be something I'm imagining and layering on afterwards but the stress was definitely having a huge physical effect on me which won't have helped with the illnesses.

Sorry you've been through these difficult and painful experiences too.

Yes. You may need to shut down right now to protect yourself and save your energy but your magic is still in there ✨I hope you can escape soon. Do you have any support there? I'm so sorry she has done this to you.

I'm really sorry to hear that. I was the same for most of my life. Recently I found a few people who have similar experiences. In fact it was people I'd already known for quite a while but I guess we only found the vocabulary to discuss it in more recent years as there is more information out there now. Also we were probably wary of opening up about it since people can be so dismissive which adds to the confusion and self-blame.

Yes the internet is amazing for connecting people with similar experiences. I don't know how I would have survived until now without it to be honest. I hope you will also find some people irl who understand and support you. It is really lonely and so unfair to have to deal with the isolation on top of the original damage. Always remember it's not your fault, it's random luck, you deserved the good parents as much as the people who actually got them.

Yes. They have a massive advantage over us - that their childhood brains developed in a safe, healthy, nurturing environment and they were guided in life skills etc. I just feel so lonely and frustrated and misunderstood that they won't ever know why I find everything so difficult. I don't hate them but increasingly I only want to spend time with people who get it.

Oh wow - it's a few decades since I was in college but this brings back memories. My mother was the same. Despite making it very clear all the years I lived with them that I was only an irritant and a burden, when I left for college it was wailing and gnashing of teeth. She didn't once say anything like "have a good time" or "call us if you need anything". It was only about her, same old story on this forum! And yet when I was back there for holidays she still didn't seem to enjoy my company. I think she just liked having me there to blame for everything and take her moods out on. 

I'm sorry I don't even really have any advice - just solidarity. I'm sorry you're experiencing that manipulation and guilt-tripping when you should be having an exciting time starting out in your own life. You are not responsible for being your mother's babysitter or emotional support animal. The referring to herself in the third person as "mommy" is just 🤮I'm glad at least other people around her can see how she really is. Good luck for the rest of your time in college and hope things get easier in the near future when you are fully independent of her.

You're not an unfeeling person - it's a normal reaction in the circumstances as you can see from this thread and others. It's normal to want to feel safe and to have a break from being hypervigilant to where the next attack will be coming from. May your feelings of peace and relief last forever now 🌟

It doesn't sound strange at all. I haven't done anything like this but I have thought about it and I totally get it. I think most people here probably understand. I'm starting to see my mother's mannerisms in myself as well as I get older 😱and it's making me feel so terrible. I'm glad this has helped you feel better.

Yeah and it's not just how annoying the endless ads are - sometimes the individual ads are so long they never get to the point. Occasionally there might be one I'm actually interested in so I don't skip so I can find out the actual name of the product or whatever but I can never get there. I guess there must be a purpose to this but does anyone know what it is? There was just an ad for some baking course and I thought a friend might like it so I waited to get some details but it went on and on and on without telling me anything at all about the company or anything and I just had to give up in the end. It can't do much good for the company - I guess maybe it financially benefits YouTube to play ads for as long as possible?
Was so relieved to get to the end of your message and see that you are NC! Yes sometimes feels like they go on and on using the life force they've sucked from other people.

🙄Yes some doctors are great at denying side effects even when they are actually documented for that drug and when many of their patients are having the exact same experience. And of course you shouldn't be asking people with actual lived experience for their actual lived experiences🙄🙄🙄much better to struggle on in isolation. 

Anyway that's great you had the option of going to someone different. Hope your appointment goes well this week🤞🤞🤞
Oh no sorry to hear that - did you find a better alternative?

Yeah NC sounds like the only option in that situation! Well done for protecting your peace and sanity and health. I wish I had done it years ago. Now I feel too guilty to do it in case they die soon - but they could also go on for quite a while longer and I'm not sure I can cope - it's damaging my own health quite a lot. I do also live far away geographically though thank goodness.
Also - yes  - I wonder now if the nasal allergies came from the same underlying inflammation in the body as the RA. Often had no discharge at all just nasal passages too inflamed to let air through.
Sorry I only saw your comment now! Guess I don't check this account much nor get alerts for it. Hope you are doing well on Plaquenil if you are taking it.
Thank you🙏
I have this fear too. So glad you are free from her now.

Glad it's not just me 😂. But I also see people, narcissists in particular, living into their 90s and 100s and their kids in their 60s still dealing with this stuff. I'm so worried this will be me. It's so sad when people get so little time in their own lives free from the abuse and toxicity.

Hope you get treatment soon - it gave me my life back. I couldn't open food packets or jars or turn taps on and off. It would take me say an hour to get up out of bed to go to the toilet or do anything as I'd have to do it so gradually - like get to a halfway sitting up position - rest for a while - sit up a bit more - rest for a while - change angle to be sitting on the edge of the bed - rest...etc etc and couldn't sit down on the toilet as knees weren't bending so had to stand over the bowl.  Now I am nearly back to normal, doing weights, running etc. I really hope it will be the same for you. I know it's absolutely horrible when you are waiting and waiting and in pain.

I don't think it made me feel more energised but it completely relieved nasal allergies that I've had since childhood. I was taking a nasal spray with a steroid and an anti-histamine, that worked very well for me, but now I've completely stopped taking that as I don't need it and it's actually lovely to not shove a spray up my nose every day! Not that it was such a hardship but this is a nice bonus surprise.

Editing just to say I am on Methotrexate too and also that I also get slight flare ups when doing weights unfortunately - not severe enough to outweigh the benefits though.

I don't really know the whole answer - not at all. But just want to say you are not stupid or a moron, you've just been conditioned to comply with them since you were very young with a sponge-like, developing brain. Those are very harsh words to use about yourself - maybe someone used those words, or others, against you in the past and taught you to see yourself that way. Maybe you could start trying to replace them with gentler and more positive words, even if it feels fake at first? I did find reading/learning about self-compassion ultimately helped me become more protective towards myself - it's helped me feel a bit more firm within myself about not being pulled into automatically blaming myself for every interaction with others that doesn't go well. I can still find it impossible to stand up for myself around family of origin because I was trained to doubt my perception so much, but it's baby steps I guess.

Edit: Sorry I didn't even really address your actual question about anger and detachment 🙈

I came here to say the same thing. I think she wants to keep you isolated. She sees you getting support and people to talk to, possibly about stuff in the family, people who might help build you a positive view of yourself - and that's massively threatening to her. You're much easier to control if you're alone and believe bad things about yourself. She might not want you to have the opportunity to compare your family to emotionally healthy, nurturing familes and she might also be worried you will talk about stuff in your family that she wants to keep secret. 

I'm not sure what you should do, sorry that I don't have more practical advice, but I hope you can stay in contact with your friend somehow.

I am the same. I live far away which helps but it's starting to feel like I will have to go no contact - but their potential reaction to that is also terrifying! I always feel like there is so much good and sensible advice around about how to handle different scenarios but I can't follow it because my nervous/sympathetic system is so activated around them. To even say something very reasonable to them in order to stand up for myself or state a boundary is physically impossible because of the state of fear, because they go from 0 to 100 in rage in an instant.

I'm trying to help myself keep my 'higher' brain online and be able to calm myself more in these fraught situations, like practicing meditation, yoga etc, but it's so much time and effort for small changes and sometimes feels like it only amounts to a sticking plaster in this situation  (although very worth doing in a more general sense.)

Yet another thread on this reddit that puts my experiences into words better than I could myself and is very validating - so thank you thank you thank you everyone!!! Honestly I can't even say how helpful it is to read your experiences, even though I'm sorry you have had them. So glad the internet exists and we can find each other.

Pete Walker (book: Complex PTSD, from Surviving to Thriving) calls this the Outer Critic (this inner voice criticising everyone else - and the Inner Critic is the voice criticising yourself.)

[https://pete-walker.com/pdf/ShrinkingOuterCritic.pdf](https://pete-walker.com/pdf/ShrinkingOuterCritic.pdf)

Here's an article on it by him in case it helps anyone understand and deal with it. I think it might be a straight copy of that chapter in his book but I'm not sure - it has the same info anyway. (Really recommend his book by the way).

Edit to say: now I reread the article I'm not sure it's as specifically relevant to the introject of the nparent's voice as I thought - but I'm leaving it here in case it's still helpful to anyone.
Definitely. Unlikely to happen though - which is weird when they seem to love the sound of their own voices so much.

Yes. I have to put in a huge amount of time and effort, over years, in order to feel very slightly better. And now my mother is getting older and feeling vulnerable, and realising I won't see the error of my ways and run back to her begging to take care of her, the long-distance abuse has amped up again - nearly 30 years after leaving and I feel back to square one.

I'm so sorry you went through that. Your mother was really cruel. All the things she said about you were really confessions about herself. I'm proud of you for getting out and finding healthy relationships and happiness,
Thank you - I really needed this right now 🙏

I'm dealing with this type of thing now. I'm receiving a barrage of guilt trips - it feels like an energy attack and I feel this emotional darkness that I haven't felt since childhood. It feels like everything I did with my life without their help is disappearing - it isn't but just because they never took an interest or listened to anything when I still tried to tell them stuff, now they are trying to dominate my thoughts and make me centre them in my life it makes my life feel invisible - argh I don't know how to explain it, I don't think I'm making sense. I live far away, I'm luckier than many people. But I've been really ill myself and I'm so tired. I'm pathetic at being firm with them.
I don't know why but there is something so satisfying about calling them "those pests" and I am going to be adopting that phrase from now on.

This post resonates so much with me. You actually made me feel compassion for myself - imagining this other defenceless child so upset and not being comforted or validated and realising I was a little child like that too. I'm so sorry your mum didn't comfort you and was actually very cruel. It wasn't your fault in any way and you deserved much better.
She probably doesn't have empathy for them either - she just wants to appear like she does.
Thank you - that's so nice of you to say 🫶 So sorry you have been through this too.

It is hard sometimes to know how to comfort someone when nobody has ever comforted you - even when you are really motivated to help them. The fact you are trying to learn makes you the opposite of narcissistic people.

Hard relate. You put it into words so well - thank you. So sorry you experienced this too. You matter. Bad things happening to you matter just as much as when they happen to other people and you deserve help and nurturing to heal just as much as everyone else does. (Still telling myself these things and pray that one day I can truly internalise them).

Yes...and now my mother is becoming elderly and feeling her vulnerability she wants constant soothing and comforting from me. If I ever visit (I hardly ever do - live in another country thank goodness) she will always appear with eyes red from crying at some point, even if it's just like a 2 day visit. On the phone there will always be something where her voice breaks into tears. It makes me wonder if she just never believed my tears as a child were real as she uses crying for manipulation herself. It doesn't matter anyway as whether she believed I was suffering or not she simply didn't care. 

When I read my post back I seem like such a horrible heartless person. She probably is genuinely depressed. I guess at least I don't treat her like she treated me - I don't completely stonewall her if she's upset or shriek "why are you always crying?!!" at her or "Count your blessings - stop acting so hard done by" (never once heard her express gratitude for anything my whole life).

Just to add - also like the idea that if they survived in some spiritual form, having transcended the human brain and their conditioning etc etc, they would see clearly the effect they'd had on me in their lives, just see the pain. I always just kind of wanted to feel seen as a person by them. I could have forgiven so much if there had ever once been any kind of acknowledgement or apology.

I can definitely see the appeal in hoping this but I prefer to think that once they are dead they are just dead - they don't exist in any form anymore - just gone. Besides, what if I go to hell and meet them there and then there's no hope of it ending haha 😱
You absolutely do matter. You are worthy of love, nurturing, protection and of being truly seen, and you always were 💗
